test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 16 May, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

I went to the lake and _______ some of its water in my metallic cup.
solution:
The correct answer is: "**drank**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past tense, so the correct verb form to use is the past simple.
 
• "**Drank**" is the past simple form of the verb "drink".
 
• The sentence demonstrates the use of parallelism, particularly in terms of verb tense.
 
• **Parallelism **is a grammatical and rhetorical device where the same grammatical structure is used for two or more parts of a sentence.
 
• In this sentence, parallelism is achieved by maintaining the past tense for both verbs, "went" and "drank."
 
• Here's a breakdown of the parallel structure:
 
 
• "I went to the lake" (past tense)
 
• "and" (connecting conjunction)
 
• "drank some of its water in my metallic cup" (past tense)
 
 
 
• The sentence indicates that the speaker took some water from the lake and consumed it, so "**drank**" is the most appropriate option.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Complete sentence**: *I went to the lake and drank __some of its water in my metallic cup. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "**Drinking**", is the present participle form of the verb "drink".
 
• "**Drunk**", is the past participle form of the verb "drink".
 
• "**Drunken**", is an adjective that describes someone who is intoxicated.
